source.title: On Visual Hallmarks of Robustness to Adversarial Malware
source.authors: Alex Huang; Abdullah Al-Dujaili; Erik Hemberg; U. O'Reilly

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied; no apparent truncation or garbling that prevents extraction.
record.tranche_reason: Extends loss-landscape and decision-map analysis to adversarially hardened malware detectors and reports results about robust generalization, a setting outside the listed claim versions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports qualitative loss-landscape and decision-map results for adversarial robustness. It does not report results on random-label fitting, natural-label train/test error gaps, or the specific measures and interventions in V1–V8. Its robust-generalization findings are recorded under fits_no_version; cited natural-generalization associations are not this paper's results.
record.test_reason: The study measures adversarial robustness and visualizes training-set loss landscapes and decision maps. These results do not test V1–V8. In particular, V7 concerns magnitude-aware sharpness ranking ordinary train/test gaps; this study uses normalized landscape plots and a robustness ranking taken from another paper, without measuring those gaps.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the authors conclude that landscape geometry may inform robust generalization, while decision-boundary locations relative to adversarial variants appear more strongly associated with robustness in their experiments. This is a qualitative comparison using a robustness ordering reported in Al-Dujaili et al. (2018), not a new quantitative generalization-gap evaluation.
record.recipe_differences: Uses adversarial training and malware feature vectors, then visualizes robust generalization; it does not use the claim's natural-label generalization setups or interventions.
record.method_sensitivity: Landscape interpretation depends on whether the loss calculation includes only variants from the model's training method or variants from all methods; decision-map results also depend on the model and variant set.

fits_no_version.finding: The three more robust hardened malware detectors have smooth, flat landscapes under both attack sets, whereas BCAk becomes more chaotic with additional attacks. Landscape plots cannot rank the three stronger models; decision-map locations follow their previously reported robustness ordering more closely.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: For these adversarially hardened malware detectors, adversarial variants' positions relative to mapped decision boundaries distinguish robustness more clearly than qualitative parameter-loss landscape geometry.

record.code_released: https://lief.quarkslab.com/ (parser URL stated; paper says visualization code will be made available upon publication, without a code URL)
record.problems: Qualitative findings are largely presented through figures and visual interpretation; exact robustness metrics and uncertainty estimates for these comparisons are not reported in the supplied text. The stated model ranking is based on cited test-set results from Al-Dujaili et al. 2018.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and the comparison with natural-label held-out accuracy.
Width-dependent test error beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD, including tuning and recovery conditions.
Batch-size effects under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Dropout's effects on held-out error across data sizes and regularization settings.
Magnitude-aware sharpness ranking ordinary train/test gaps among comparably fitted convolutional networks, and comparison with norm- and margin-based measures.
Test-accuracy effects of removing memorized examples versus random examples.

record.verdict_notes: The Figure 5 caption contains inconsistent panel references and a flatness description that conflicts with the main text's description of BCAk. The row values follow Sections 3.3–3.4. No result warrants a verdict on V1–V8.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label test accuracy.
Width sweeps and test error beyond interpolation.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD held-out performance.
The paper considers loss-landscape flatness in relation to robust generalization, but does not measure the magnitude-aware sharpness and same-distribution train/test gap specified in this version.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring test accuracy.

rows.subject: Natural
rows.operation_detail: Compared parameter loss landscapes using benign and malicious samples plus the union of adversarial variants from all four methods.
rows.measure: Loss-landscape geometry as an indicator of robust generalization
rows.value: The loss landscape has a chaotic structure with adversarial variants from all inner maximizers.
rows.note: The paper describes this as supporting a distinction between standard and robust generalization; it does not report a natural train/test error gap.
rows.check: The reported chaotic landscape concerns adversarial robustness, not any version's effect.

rows.subject: dFGSMk
rows.operation_detail: Compared parameter loss landscapes using the training method's variants and using variants from all four methods.
rows.measure: Loss-landscape flatness and smoothness in relation to robust generalization
rows.value: Flatness and smoothness persist in both landscape conditions.
rows.note: The authors group dFGSMk with the top three robust hardened models.
rows.check: Qualitative landscape flatness is reported correctly, but no ordinary generalization gap or V7 ranking measure is evaluated.

rows.subject: BCAk
rows.operation_detail: Compared parameter loss landscapes using the training method's variants and using variants from all four methods.
rows.measure: Loss-landscape geometry in relation to robust generalization
rows.value: A small bump appears near the model's parameters.
rows.note: The paper describes BCAk as poorly hardened.
rows.check: A small landscape bump does not establish a partial effect for any version. The value matches Section 3.3.

rows.subject: BCAk
rows.operation_detail: Compared parameter loss landscapes using the training method's variants and using variants from all four methods.
rows.measure: Loss-landscape geometry in relation to robust generalization
rows.baseline: model-dataset landscape: a small bump near the model's parameters
rows.value: The landscape becomes more chaotic when the other adversarial variants are incorporated.
rows.note: The paper identifies BCAk as poorly hardened.
rows.check: Changing the attack set changes landscape geometry; this does not measure any version's effect.

rows.subject: Natural
rows.operation_detail: Mapped decision regions and overlaid adversarial variants from all four methods.
rows.measure: Locations of adversarial variants relative to regions classified benign or malicious
rows.value: Most adversarial variants lie in regions assigned to the benign class with high confidence.
rows.note: This is a decision-map result about adversarial robustness, not same-distribution natural-label generalization.
rows.check: The decision map shows adversarial misclassification, not an effect specified by V1–V8.

rows.subject: rFGSMk
rows.operation_detail: Mapped decision regions and overlaid variants generated by the training method.
rows.measure: Adversarial-variant locations relative to the benign/malicious decision boundary
rows.value: The variants sit relatively far from the decision boundary compared with the other hardened models.
rows.note: The paper calls rFGSMk the most robust model.
rows.check: Mapped adversarial variants' distance from a decision boundary does not measure any version's effect.

rows.note: The count is approximate as stated in the paper.
rows.check: The approximate visual count matches the text, but is not a held-out error rate or a measure of any version's effect.
